entries.name: The Watch That Never Ends
entries.summary: A kingdom sleeps because someone stays awake.
entries.lore:
In the winter of the Unlit Road, the Crown sent its soldiers home before the mountain passes closed. One gate captain refused to draw the bar. Three wagons were still missing, and she knew the names of the drivers. Her company carried lanterns into the snow. At dawn they returned with frost-blackened hands, two broken axles, and every traveler accounted for.

The Crown Guard still calls its evening muster the Counting of Lights. A recruit learns the roads, the households, and the sound of trouble before earning a place at the gate. There are sword drills until the wrists ache, long patrols in weather no one remembers, and quiet decisions made with a frightened stranger watching. Their authority is measured by how safely another person can pass beneath it.

When war comes, those same soldiers march at the front of the Crownlands. They know what lies behind the walls because they have kept watch over it. At each change of guard, one lantern passes from hand to hand. The soldier may rest. The watch goes on.
entries.effect: A trained melee soldier, equipped with sword and shield to defend the settlement.

entries.name: When the Bells Call
entries.summary: Every bell has a voice. Every village has an answer.
entries.lore:
The first militia roll was written on the back of a baker’s account book. Raiders had cut the road, the garrison was two days away, and the village bell was ringing. A cooper brought a wooden shield. A mason carried an iron mace from the storehouse. One by one, names usually called across a market square answered from behind the barricade.

The Crown later sent weapons, instructors, and a banner. The villagers kept the book. Its pages taught each new company that courage needed practice: how to brace a shield, keep a weapon clear of a neighbor, and carry the wounded through a narrow door. They trained after work and before harvest, until the bell could call a company instead of a frightened crowd.

Their armor is plain, their shields repaired more often than replaced. But every lane has a name they know, and every rooftop shelters someone who will wait for them. When the bells call, they come with trembling hands and familiar faces. They come because the person beside them came too.
entries.effect: A lightly armored melee defender, fighting with mace and shield.
